title: Performance commitments, credit formula, and measurement spec for Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Draft a defensible, measurable contract and internal spec for Dedicated capacity performance commitments. Deliverables: (1) formal metric definitions (what we measure and how), (2) credit calculation formula for customer remediation, (3) interaction model with autoscaling and scheduled maintenance windows, and (4) sample contract wording for legal/enterprise sales.
acceptance_criteria: Metric definitions specify exact telemetry sources, aggregation windows, and handling for missing/partial telemetry
Credit calculation example tables for 3 common failure modes (capacity throttling, regional outage, scheduled maintenance) validated by Finance and Legal
Autoscale interplay documented: how credits change when autoscale policy triggers vs manual scale decisions
Draft contract language (customer-facing) reviewed and approved by Legal and Sales engineering
Measurement edge-cases and dispute resolution process captured with owner assignments
technical_notes: Primary metric: sustained served tokens/sec per committed GPU-equivalent over a rolling 1h window and 30d window for long-term commitments
Latency SLOs will be percentile-based (p95/p99) tied to token throughput buckets; throughput SLO defined as tokens delivered within configured latency envelope
Error budget: defined in token-seconds lost relative to committed baseline; mapped to dollar credits via a linear scale with step-down thresholds
Telemetry sources: runtime token counters (serve pipeline), GPU utilization events, autoscaler decisions log, infra incident markers (region/outage tags)
Measurement windows: primary (1h rolling for immediate detection), billing (30d window aligned to customer billing cycle), and dispute window (90d lookback for evidence)

risks: Telemetry gaps during regional outages may undercount or misattribute lost throughput; mitigation: pair token counters with region outage markers and fall back to capacity model estimates
Autoscale-induced variability could make short-term measurement noisy; mitigation: use 1h sustained windows and require multi-hour breaches before issuing credits
Legal appetite for high credit caps may exceed business risk tolerances; mitigate with capped total-credits per contract and gradual remediation (service credits vs termination rights)
Customers with aggressive autoscale settings might trigger credits even when behavior is deliberate; include customer-configured policy attribution in dispute flow
notes_for_engineering: Eng to provide a reproducible measurement job (script + sample data) that outputs per-customer tokens/sec and p95/p99 latency over the measurement windows. Include synthetic replay test to simulate outages for validation.
contract_snippets: Service Commitment: Redwood will make available Dedicated capacity that provides a sustained throughput equal to the Customer's committed tokens-per-second (TPS) for the duration of the Term, measured on a rolling 1-hour basis and reconciled monthly.

Credit Formula (summary): If realized sustained TPS < 95% of committed TPS for > 3 continuous hours within a 30-day billing cycle, Customer is eligible for a Service Credit equal to min(25% of monthly committed fees, $C), where $C is computed as (Committed TPS - Realized TPS) / Committed TPS * Monthly Fee. Full formula and cap table included in Appendix A.

Measurement Exceptions: Scheduled maintenance windows announced >= 72 hours in advance and totaling <= 6 hours per 30-day period will not be eligible for credits. Force majeure events and third-party network outages are excluded per Section X.

Dispute Process: Customer must open a billing dispute within 90 days of the suspected breach with supporting evidence. Redwood will provide telemetry export and a runbook-level explanation of attribution within 10 business days. If telemetry is insufficient, Redwood may use modeled estimates for credit calculation.
open_questions: Should we index the credit cap to contract size (e.g., fixed cap vs sliding cap)? Legal prefers fixed caps; Finance prefers sliding to manage risk — need decision
What default autoscale attribution model should we use when both customer and Redwood autoscalers act in the same window? (priority: attribute to customer actions unless clearly caused by infra)
How to handle fractional GPUs and cross-tenant oversubscription in committed calculations? Should we normalize to 'GPU-equivalent' metric?
